newsitem.title: UK: UK building societies under pressure - Datamonitor.
newsitem.headline: UK building societies under pressure - Datamonitor.

text.p: British building societies are facing one of the toughest periods in their 150-year history with some 50 percent of assets deserting the sector and new competitors making inroads into their traditional market.
A report from Datamonitor said many of the dominant and influential societies will be leaving the sector in the next two years.

"Societies' core markets are in trouble and in order to compete the smaller societies will need to rethink their strategies, either as individuals or alliances," said Datamonitor consultant Richard Spencer.

The report said that by the end of 1997 the sector will have lost the Halifax, Alliance & Leicester, the Northern Rock, Bristol and West "and a handful of other building societies",adding up to more than half of total assets.
The remaining top five players -- Nationwide, Bradford & Bingley, Britannia, Birmingham Midshires and Yorkshire will account for 60 percent of building society assets.
Datamonitor also sees no growth in the mortgage market for the next five years, putting pressure on revenue earned from mortgages by the societies.
"Many will be unable to survive this period and will be taken over possibly (and in fact probably) by their former allies, the newly demutualised societies," the report said.
